answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network employs Stake-Bonded TPM Attestation. First, every agent must lock $7,500 in a slashing escrow. Second, the local hardware TPM generates a verifiable, unique cryptographic signature. Third, the protocol validates this signature against the locked bond. Fourth, any detected identity fraud results in immediate asset forfeiture. An attacker would face a cost of $7,500 per identity and 12 hours of hardware initialization. This mechanism acts like a heavy sable cloak anchoring a traveler to a stone jetty amidst a dark, swirling plume of smoke.
